anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Costing inputs (row counts, histograms, correlations) are stale or absent, driving systematic cardinality misestimation and sub-optimal plan selection.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Access to popular buffer pages is serialized by heavy latch or pin waits, causing sessions to stall or spin while competing for the same in-memory blocks.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes saturate host CPU, exhausting scheduler capacity and inflating run-queue and context-switch overhead regardless of the logical origin of the demand.

When these three root causes strike concurrently, the workload exhibits a mixture of misleading estimates, acute page-level hot spots, and full CPU saturation. Queries whose plans were already risky because of wrong statistics may choose nested-loop joins on underestimated result sets or full scans on underestimated large tables; both inflate logical I/O, repeatedly touch a small set of root or bitmap pages, and amplify latch waits. Sessions spin on buffer latches, inflating CPU consumption without progressing work, driving overall host utilization to 100 %. As CPU headroom disappears, latency balloons across the instance, autovacuum or automatic-statistics jobs fall further behind, and wait-event dashboards show alternating bursts of “latch: buffer busy”, “CPU run queue”, and “cardinality feedback” events, making the true culprit hard to pinpoint.

Causally, stale or missing statistics (1) misdirect the optimizer into plans that concentrate reads or writes on a few pages. This creates artificial hot pages that (2) trigger buffer-cache latch contention; the spin-loop behavior of those latches (3) burns CPU cycles, escalating the CPU Resource Anomaly. In turn, CPU starvation delays background I/O writers and statistics jobs, allowing statistics to grow even staler and hot pages to stay longer in cache, which perpetuates the latch conflict. Thus all three anomalies form a reinforcing feedback loop that degrades throughput far more severely than any single anomaly in isolation.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a source/replica connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: A replica waits longer than replica_net_timeout for more data from the source connection.
entry.workload_impact: The replication network read is aborted and the replica considers the connection interrupted.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
